log: CAN A STRUCTURAL DISCRIMINATOR FIND A CATALYST? -- the arithmetic that decides the design
The mechanism is right: unlike co-dependency and co-expression, a binding calculation asks
'does this enzyme act on this substrate', which IS the question. So the issue is not whether
the signal is relevant. It is whether the signal is SHARP ENOUGH for the size of the search.
Candidate enzyme vocabulary: 5,282 genes.
WHERE THE TRUE CATALYST LANDS, by discriminator quality and shortlist size
(expected rank of the true catalyst; a screen is only useful if this is single digits)
discriminator                           AUC       N=5      N=10      N=20      N=50     N=200    N=1000    N=5282
GeoConv, interface point pairs        0.617       2.5       4.4       8.3      19.8      77.2     383.6    2023.6
dMaSIF surface descriptor, unbound    0.714       2.1       3.6       6.4      15.0      57.9     286.7    1511.4
NEXUS dual sensor (fold x bind)       0.755       2.0       3.2       5.7      13.0      49.8     245.8    1294.8
THE AUC A FULL SCREEN WOULD REQUIRE
to place the true catalyst in the top 1   of 5,282:  AUC >= 1.0000
to place the true catalyst in the top 5   of 5,282:  AUC >= 0.9992
to place the true catalyst in the top 10  of 5,282:  AUC >= 0.9983
to place the true catalyst in the top 50  of 5,282:  AUC >= 0.9907
best measured in this project: 0.814 (best docking rescore) -- short by 0.184
READING
NEXUS CANNOT BE THE SEARCH. Screening 5,282 enzymes needs AUC 0.9983 to reach a
top-10; the best structural number this project has measured is 0.814, which leaves the
true catalyst near rank 983. That is the same wall the
docking line already hit seven different ways -- generation worked, ranking did not -- and
nothing about spheres or a third protein changes the size of the candidate space.
NEXUS AS A TIE-BREAK IS A DIFFERENT PROPOSITION, and the arithmetic supports it. On a shortlist
of  5: AUC 0.814 puts the true catalyst at expected rank 1.7, and the NEXUS sensor at 2.0
of 10: AUC 0.814 puts the true catalyst at expected rank 2.7, and the NEXUS sensor at 3.2
of 20: AUC 0.814 puts the true catalyst at expected rank 4.5, and the NEXUS sensor at 5.7
which is exactly the regime where a physics score can convert a near-miss into a hit.
AND THIS SESSION ALREADY BUILT THE SHORTLIST GENERATOR. Closed-book naming reaches 0.463 top-1
on the obscure enzymes that make up the gap; its top-10 will be well above that. So the
composition the numbers support is:
LLM proposes ~10 candidates  ->  structure/NEXUS discriminates within them
That is the original instinct applied at the N where the physics can actually pay, and it is
the design the pilot should test. What it needs measured next, in order:
1. top-10 accuracy of the closed-book arm (is the answer even in the shortlist?)
2. AUC of the binding score on true-catalyst vs 9 decoys, with AlphaFold structures
3. whether 1 and 2 compose, against the 0.463 top-1 the LLM already delivers alone
Step 2 is only worth running if step 1 clears roughly 0.7 -- otherwise the discriminator is
sorting a list that does not contain the answer, which is the 0.505 ceiling all over again.
SCOPE, measured separately: of the 9,186 enzyme-shaped gaps, 2,143 (23%) have a protein or
complex participant to dock against. The other 7,043 are metabolite-in-a-pocket, a different
calculation than the protein-protein one NEXUS performs.
